heading: INT. GRAND HOTEL PARLOUR, SARATOGA - 1893 - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. GRAND HOTEL PARLOUR, SARATOGA - 1893 - AFTERNOON
A tea table laid for three.
Gilded mirrors.
A potted fern quivers in a draught from the verandah doors.
MRS. CORNELIA VANDERHOOF-ADEBAYO, 50s, rigid in black silk, presides over the pot.
Her niece MISS BEATRIX ONWUACHI-LAW, 20s, in lavender, pleats a napkin.
Across from them sits MADAME SOLANGE TREMBLAY-OKORO, 40s, a visitor, gloved and veiled, smiling thinly.
Sugar, Madame?
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: One lump.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: Beatrix, the tongs.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Yes, Aunt.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: She never listens. You will find that of the young.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: I find it of the old as well.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: I beg your pardon?
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Nothing at all. The tea is excellent.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: It is from Ceylon.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: I should never have guessed. I took it for Darjeeling.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: Aunt prides herself on knowing the difference.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Beatrix.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Only as an observation.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Observation is a great virtue, Miss Onwuachi-Law. Tell me, what do you observe about this room?
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: The mirrors are very bright.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: And?
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: The draught is not from the verandah.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Beatrix, do not be absurd.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: It is from behind the fern.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: I find your niece quite remarkable.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: She finds herself so.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Mrs. Vanderhoof-Adebayo, when your husband died so suddenly in the spring, the physician said it was his heart.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: It was.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: And yet, the family lawyer tells me the will has been altered.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: Naturally. Estates are tidied.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Altered in your favour.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: Madame Tremblay-Okoro, I invited you for tea, not for an inquest.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: But it is a tea, is it not? And teas, in my experience, are where the truth is poured.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: Beatrix drops the tongs.
The silver clatters on the china.
Nobody moves to retrieve them.
Aunt?
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Be quiet, child.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Let her speak. She has been waiting two seasons.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: Cornelia lifts the teapot.
Her hand is perfectly steady.
She pours, and the stream falls straight and gold into the empty cup before her.
You are very sure of yourself.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: I am Pinkerton's agent in New York.
units.name: SOLANGE

units.text: Behind the fern, a floorboard creaks.
The draught stops.
